tagline: Everything in order before and after you land
housingAlert: Never pay a deposit or rent before you have seen the room (in person or on a live video call) and signed a contract.
Be wary of prices far below the area average, owners who are 'abroad', and requests to pay by money-transfer apps.
You will need the contract or another document proving you live there to register on the padrón: check you will get one before paying.
Ask your university's international office before paying anything.

tasks.title: Admission and tuition paid
tasks.description: For a study stay you must be admitted by a recognised higher-education institution to a full-time programme leading to a recognised degree, and have paid the registration or enrolment fees. The consulate asks for proof of both.
steps: Accept your offer
Pay the registration or enrolment fees
Ask the university for the admission letter for your visa
tasks.officialSourceName: Ministerio de Inclusión – Hoja 1: Estancia por estudios

tasks.title: Health insurance valid in Spain
tasks.description: You need health insurance with an insurer authorised to operate in Spain, with cover similar to the Spanish National Health System's common basic services. Proof of it is part of the visa application.
steps: Choose a policy from an insurer authorised in Spain
Check the cover matches the public system's basic services
Keep the certificate for the visa
tasks.officialSourceName: Ministerio de Inclusión – Hoja 1: Estancia por estudios

tasks.title: Proof of sufficient funds
tasks.description: Show enough money to live and return home: each month, 100% of IPREM (Spain's public income reference), unless you prove your accommodation is paid in advance for the whole stay. Money used for tuition does not count.
documentsNeeded: Bank statements, scholarship letter or sponsor documents
steps: Calculate the amount for your months of study
Gather bank statements or scholarship proof
If your housing is prepaid, keep proof of it
tasks.officialSourceName: Ministerio de Inclusión – Hoja 1: Estancia por estudios
tasks.todo: TODO: verify the current monthly IPREM amount on an official source before showing a figure.

tasks.title: Criminal record certificate
tasks.description: If your stay is longer than six months and you are of legal age, bring a criminal record certificate from your country of origin or the countries where you lived in the last five years. Foreign documents must be legalised or apostilled and translated into Spanish by a sworn translator.
steps: Request the certificate in each country
Get it apostilled or legalised
Have it translated by a sworn translator
tasks.officialSourceName: Ministerio de Inclusión – Hoja 1: Estancia por estudios

tasks.title: Medical certificate
tasks.description: When you apply from outside Spain, bring a medical certificate stating you have none of the diseases with serious public-health impact under the 2005 International Health Regulations.
documentsNeeded: Sworn translation if not in Spanish
steps: Book a doctor's appointment
Ask for the certificate wording required
Translate it if needed
tasks.officialSourceName: Ministerio de Inclusión – Hoja 1: Estancia por estudios

tasks.title: Student visa
tasks.description: Apply in person at the Spanish embassy or consulate for where you live, at least two months before your studies start. Your passport must be valid for at least one year. The consulate has up to one month to decide, and once granted you must collect the visa within two months.
documentsNeeded: Passport valid for at least 1 year
steps: Book at the Spanish consulate for your place of residence
Apply at least 2 months before your studies start
Collect the visa within 2 months of the decision
tasks.officialSourceName: Ministerio de Inclusión – Hoja 1: Estancia por estudios

tasks.cost: Visa fee, paid when you apply (amount not verified)
tasks.deadline: Apply at least 2 months before your studies start

tasks.title: Accommodation in Madrid
tasks.description: Find a room or flat and sign a contract. You will need a document proving you live there to register on the padrón. Housing scams are the most common problem students report: read the alert before paying.
steps: Shortlist offers with your university's housing service
View the room or do a live video call
Sign and keep every receipt
tasks.todo: TODO: verify official guidance on rental contracts and deposits in the Comunidad de Madrid.
tasks.warning: Housing scams: never pay before seeing the room and signing a contract.

tasks.title: Foreigner identity card (TIE)
tasks.description: If your study stay is longer than six months, apply in person for the TIE within one month of entering Spain, at the police station or foreigners' office where you live. You fill in form EX-17 and pay fee form 790, code 012 at a bank before the appointment.
documentsNeeded: Photo and documents listed by the police
steps: Get an appointment (cita previa) for fingerprints / TIE
Pay fee 790-012 at a bank before going
Attend in person and collect the card later
tasks.officialSourceName: Policía Nacional – Tarjeta estudiante para extranjeros

tasks.title: Address registration
tasks.description: Everyone who lives in Spain must register on the padrón of the municipality where they usually live. In Madrid you can do it online, or in person with a mandatory appointment at a Línea Madrid citizen office. The registration certificate is free.
documentsNeeded: Residence card, or passport if you do not have it yet
Document proving you use the home (e.g. rental contract)
steps: Prepare the hoja padronal and your housing document
Register online or book an appointment at a Línea Madrid office
Request your free padrón certificate
tasks.officialSourceName: Ayuntamiento de Madrid – Padrón Municipal: empadronamiento

tasks.title: Bank account
tasks.description: Banks in Spain must offer a basic payment account without making you buy other products. It covers opening and closing the account, deposits, cash withdrawals, and payments in the EU: direct debits, debit or prepaid card payments (including online) and transfers.
documentsNeeded: Documents the bank asks for about your situation
steps: Ask a bank for a basic payment account
Bring valid identity documents
Answer the bank's questions about your situation
tasks.officialSourceName: Banco de España – ¿Qué es la cuenta de pago básica?

tasks.title: Young transport pass
tasks.description: A personal 30-day pass with unlimited journeys across all fare zones (A to E2), from age 15 until you turn 26. It costs 10 euros and is loaded onto the personal public transport card (Tarjeta Transporte Público Personal).
steps: Get the personal public transport card
Load the Abono Joven
Recharge every 30 days
tasks.officialSourceName: Consorcio Regional de Transportes de Madrid – Abono Joven

tasks.title: Health insurance (EHIC)
tasks.description: EU citizens use the European Health Insurance Card for medically necessary care during a temporary stay. It is free and you request it from your own insurer before leaving.
steps: Request the EHIC before you travel
tasks.officialSourceName: Your Europe – Health cover for temporary stays

tasks.title: Extend your stay
tasks.localName: Prórroga de la autorización de estancia
tasks.description: If your studies continue, you can apply to extend the authorisation. Check the conditions and the deadline on the official sheet well before your card expires.
steps: Read the extension section of the official sheet
Apply before your authorisation expires
tasks.officialSourceName: Ministerio de Inclusión – Hoja 1: Estancia por estudios
